note: CURATED. Figures are the manufacturer-published ones for the era each car represents: tank capacity, combined consumption, kerb weight and top speed. Names are original — this is a game about an unsanctioned race and no manufacturer would licence it, so nothing here is meant to be a real marque. What each car DOES is derived in scripts/lib/cars.mjs, which is modelled and labelled as such.

categories.executive: Executive autocruisers — the meta picks. Huge top speed, big boots for auxiliary tanks, and styling that vanishes into traffic.
categories.poster: Poster supercars — unbeatable top end, maximum police attention, small tanks and fragile nerves.
categories.camouflage: Camouflaged utilities — trade aerodynamics for hiding in plain sight, or for actively deceiving enforcement.
categories.tuner: Tuner platforms — the baselines people build endless-highway cars out of.
categories.wildcard: Alternative-tech wildcards — a huge advantage in one place bought with a huge cost somewhere else.

cars.name: Nordstern Kurier 63
cars.notes: Peak twin-turbo V8 saloon. The default answer, and the one every regulation is written to constrain.

cars.name: Vierring Sechs S
cars.notes: Limited to 250 as delivered. Anonymous to the point of invisibility, which is the entire point.

cars.name: Weissblau M540 Competition
cars.notes: All-wheel drive and long-stint composure. Smallest tank of the four.

cars.name: Zuffen Panorama Turbo S
cars.notes: The biggest tank in the class paired with the highest top speed. Heavy, and drinks accordingly.

cars.name: Toro Stregone LP400S
cars.notes: Enormous tank, appalling consumption, and every camera on the continent looks at it.

cars.name: Cavallo 512 BR
cars.notes: Flat-twelve built for sustained autostrada cruising rather than for corners.

cars.name: Crossflag Ray Z6
cars.notes: Mid-engined and high-revving. No boot worth the name, so no auxiliary tank.

cars.name: Zuffen 992 Turbo S
cars.notes: The supercar that behaves like an executive saloon in weather. Small tank is the price.

cars.name: Ramhorn Fieldsman Ambulance
cars.notes: Slow and thirsty, with a tank that hides the fact. Deception only pays once enforcement exists.

cars.name: Sierra Works C-35 Dually
cars.notes: The longest range in the game and the lowest cruise speed. A pure range experiment.

cars.name: Dearborn Regent Interceptor
cars.notes: Blends into North American traffic and stands out badly in Europe. Kept as the contrast case.

cars.name: Ironmark V90 Crossroad
cars.notes: The European answer to the whole category: a fast estate that nobody looks at twice.

cars.name: Dearborn Colt GT
cars.notes: Strip the rear seats and it takes a fuel cell bigger than the original tank.

cars.name: Kure RZ-7
cars.notes: Light and thirsty. Trades frequent stops for a car that does everything else well.

cars.name: Aichi Sovra Turbo
cars.notes: Limited from the factory and overbuilt underneath. The obvious derestrict candidate.

cars.name: Crossflag Cambria ZL1
cars.notes: Adaptive damping, which is what keeps the speed up on bad surfaces rather than on smooth ones.

cars.name: Weissblau 535d
cars.notes: The efficiency benchmark. On a long race this is very hard to beat.

cars.name: Leaper XJ-R
cars.notes: Supercharged sleeper. Comfortable at pace, and the reliability system will not be kind to it.

cars.name: Meridian LS 400
cars.notes: Unremarkable at everything and immune to the thing that ends other people's races.

cars.name: Ampere S Tri-Motor
cars.notes: Needs its own stop model: fewer, far longer stops, and charger density in Europe varies from saturated in Norway to sparse in the Balkans. amenity=charging_station is in OSM, so it is importable. The only candidate left that is coupled to PLACE rather than to road class.
